beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new, it's a title

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: you share context, a skill, output or an interface, never the agent itself. my engineers copy whole repos around, so this is new to me

beats.trigger: Bring one example from your own organisation where people got access to a tool and did not use it.
beats.got: homework. i have an example (our notion rollout), so ok

beats.trigger: **Interview** for a teammate's job before choosing what to share
beats.got: nothing new, a list of verbs. the interview step sounds like ceremony to me

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to have: your `memory/` folder, one of your skills, the morning output, or a way to ask the agent a question in Slack?
beats.got: i'd say the slack bot, because i want it out of my terminal. fine, let's go

beats.trigger: Hold the impulse. Then start with the teammate's work.
beats.got: don't build first, ask what the teammate needs. fair, but i already have the sales team in mind

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: the agent reads my files and guesses the teammate's job. mine came out generic, so i just rewrote it myself. didn't reread it much

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: that's exactly how i pick things. i pick what fits our stack. fair hit, a bit annoying

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new, a handoff to the next exercise

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: two plans, technical and people. i only ever do the technical one

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: find the one obstacle that keeps the others hard. my agent said trust in who maintains it. i hadn't thought about that, and it's org-level stuff, which is what i came for

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: my people plan was mostly UNASSIGNED. that is my sales weekend build: nobody owns it. uncomfortable, and useful

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans, imagines the failure, and writes the first real-world contact
beats.got: nothing new, a pointer to the next exercise

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: treat the plans as guesses until tested. true, but i'd still rather build and see

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: flip the question from how do i get adoption to what makes them switch. the sales team's current tool is a spreadsheet and a colleague. my thing is competing with that

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: premortem as three failure stories. the strongest one was that nobody maintains it and it quietly dies. i'd have hit that

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: picking by fit to infra is shopping, picking by outcome is design. i'll steal that for my architecture reviews

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new, a title

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute.
beats.got: licence numbers and real use are different things. i know it, we report seats, not use. good line anyway

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: antti built a good multi-agent analysis and leadership didn't decide, because they hadn't done the thinking themselves. real story, no hype, and it fits how my own exec team behaves

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all, which is why the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts, with the fourth still sitting with whoever built it.
beats.got: you can copy context, boundary and checks. you can't copy the person who answers for it. that's why my side project gets nowhere outside engineering

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: mostly a recap of the four strategies, with what each asks of the receiver. mildly useful

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.
beats.got: switching needs it to land where they look, be right the first time, and have a trusted person vouch for it. so for sales it can't be me, it has to be someone in sales

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: talk to one person before building more. slightly annoying, since building is what i do on weekends. i see why though

beats.trigger: It is rarely the same person across all four.
beats.got: different people want different shapes. fine, i let the agent make the artifact and skimmed it

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.
beats.got: nothing new, a summary of what i just did

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: bring back what the person said. ok

beats.trigger: What if you didn't have to build each one by hand?
beats.got: teaser for automating agent building. that's what i actually want, so i'm in

take_homes: my sales-team build has no owner and nobody asked for it. the unnamed maintainer is the real blocker, not the tech
ask what would make a person switch from their spreadsheet or colleague, and don't pick the shape because it fits our stack
you can copy context, checks and the boundary, but the person who answers for it doesn't copy

monday.move: ask one sales lead how they prepare for a customer call today, and park the weekend build until they answer
monday.who: one sales lead, not the whole team
monday.when: Monday, before the build goes any further
monday.stop_condition: if they say the current spreadsheet is fine, or nobody in sales will own it, i stop
monday.blocker: i'll want to build it anyway, and i still don't know who would maintain it

misconception.why: the unnamed roles in my own people plan showed that a good agent doesn't make a good rollout. but this was about ownership, not checking agent output, and i still skipped the review step in the exercises. only partly shaken

one_line: it didn't teach me anything about agents, but it told me why my weekend build for sales would have died, and the story about leadership not deciding is one i'll pass on.
